info.name: BPMSquare API v1 - Quotations
info.description:
Full CRUD over **quotations** on the BPMSquare v1 REST API, with worked examples
on every request.

---

# Getting started

1. Import this collection **and** the environment file next to it.
2. Generate a key: **Admin → Tenants → *your tenant* → External API key**.
3. Paste it into the environment's `api_key` variable (empty and marked secret).
4. Point `base_url` at the environment you mean to hit.

| Environment | `base_url` |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://bpmsquare-app-git-develop-munira1.vercel.app/api/v1` |
| Production — Vikas Pioneers | `https://vikas.bpmsquare.com/api/v1` |
| Production — Demo tenant | `https://app.bpmsquare.com/api/v1` |

Run the **Setup** folder first — its last request captures an `account_id` into
the environment, which the create requests depend on.

---

# Authentication

```
Authorization: Bearer <tenant API key>
```

Set once at collection level, so every request inherits it.

The key both authenticates the caller **and selects the tenant** — there is no
tenant or account id in any URL. A key issued for Vikas Pioneers can only ever
see and touch Vikas Pioneers data.

> ⚠️ **The key grants writes, not just reads.** It can create, modify and delete
> quotations. Treat it like a password: keep it in the Postman environment,
> never in the collection body or a shared export, and regenerate it in Admin
> if it leaks.

---

# Conventions

**Money is always calculated server-side.** Sending `total` on a quotation or
`amount` on a line is a `422` — not silently ignored.

```
line amount = qty × rate × (1 − discount_pct/100)
subtotal    = Σ amount of effective lines
total       = subtotal − header discount − material deductions
```

*Effective lines* excludes lines in an `alternative` group other than the one
named by `selected_option_id` — options the customer did not take.

**Tax is not part of `total`.** `gst_rate` is applied at display and print time.
The detail response carries a `totals` breakdown so you can reconcile.

**Unknown fields are rejected, not ignored.** A typo fails with `422` naming the
field. A bulk load should fail on row 1, not silently drop a column across ten
thousand rows.

**Child arrays are replaced wholesale.** Sending `lines` on a PATCH discards the
existing set. Always send the complete array; omit the key to leave lines alone.

**Line ordering is natural, not lexicographic.** `sl_no` is text (so `1a` and
`2.10` work) but sorts numerically on read — `1, 2, 10`, never `1, 10, 2`.

**Every write is audited.** Creates, updates and deletes appear in
Administration → Change History with actor `api:v1`.

---

# The date profile

Six dates, behaving differently. This matters if you are backfilling history.

| Field | Type | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Row creation. Read-only. |
| `quote_date` | date | Business date on the document. Yours; back-dating is fine. |
| `inquiry_date` | date | When the customer asked. Never auto-stamped. |
| `submitted_at` | timestamp | Auto-stamped when the quote first leaves its initial status, and on an email send. **Override by sending a value.** |
| `closed_at` | timestamp | Auto-stamped when `outcome` leaves `open`; cleared if it returns. **Override by sending a value.** |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Maintained on every write. Read-only. |

Auto-stamps fire on **PATCH only, never POST** — so a historical import can state
its own `submitted_at` and `closed_at` and the server will not overwrite them.

---

# Errors

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Body is not valid JSON |
| `401` | Missing or unrecognised API key |
| `404` | Not found in your tenant, or a referenced id is not yours |
| `422` | Validation failed — see `details[]` |
| `500` | Server or database error |

A `422` reports every problem at once, so one pass fixes a row.

---

# Limits

- 200 lines per quotation per request
- No pagination on `GET /quotations` yet
- No rate limiting yet
- No per-line endpoint — lines are managed through the parent quotation

---

Field-level reference: `GET {{base_url}}/metadata/quotations`, or `API_V1.md`
in the repo.

Five create variants show the range: minimal, typical, every-writable-field, grouped/alternatives, and a technical (no-pricing) offer.

Safe to run repeatedly — the last two requests delete what the folder created.

request.description:
A realistic quotation with three line items.

**What to notice in the response:**
- `ref` is generated server-side using the tenant's Quote ID format — you never supply it.
- `total` is `145000 + 16200 + 7500 = 168700`. The second line's `discount_pct: 10` is applied per line before the total.
- `sl_no` `"10"` comes back **after** `"2"`, not between `"1"` and `"2"`.
- `quote_date` keeps the back-dated value rather than snapping to today.

{
  "account_id": "{{account_id}}",
  "name": "Rewinding of 180 kW motor",
  "type": "quotation",
  "quote_date": "2026-04-09",
  "valid_until": "2026-05-09",
  "inquiry_date": "2026-04-01",

Note `submitted_at` is supplied here: on **POST** the server never auto-stamps it, so a historical import lands exactly the dates it states.

request.description:
The harder shape: an **alternative** Option A / Option B pair the customer chooses between, plus a **material salvage deduction**.

Lines sharing a `group_id` form a group. `group_type: "alternative"` makes groups mutually exclusive — only the one named by `selected_option_id` counts:

```
  12000   base work
+ 145000  Option A (selected)
     ---  Option B 78000 quoted but excluded
-  18000  copper salvage (category: material)
= 139000
```

Use `group_type: "additive"` instead when every group should count.

body.raw:
{
  "account_id": "{{account_id}}",
  "name": "Motor repair \u2014 options quote",
  "selected_option_id": "opt-a",
  "lines": [
    {
      "sl_no": "1",
      "description": "Dismantling and inspection",
      "uom": "Job",
      "qty": 1,
      "rate": 12000
    },
    {
      "sl_no": "2.1",
      "description": "Full rewind with F-class insulation",
      "uom": "Nos",
      "qty": 1,
      "rate": 145000,
      "group_id": "opt-a",
      "group_label": "Option A - Full rewind",
      "group_type": "alternative",
      "group_description": "Complete replacement of stator winding"
    },
    {
      "sl_no": "2.2",
      "description": "Partial rewind, damaged coils only",
      "uom": "Nos",
      "qty": 1,
      "rate": 78000,
      "group_id": "opt-b",
      "group_label": "Option B - Partial rewind",
      "group_type": "alternative"
    },
    {
      "sl_no": "3",
      "description": "Copper scrap recovered",
      "uom": "Kg",
      "qty": 40,
      "rate": 0,
      "category": "material",
      "deduction": 18000
    }
  ]
}

exec: pm.test('unselected option excluded from total', () => pm.expect(q.total).to.eql(139000));
pm.test('but option B is still stored', () => pm.expect(q.lines.length).to.eql(4));

response.name: 201 Created

Lines sharing a `group_id` form a group. `group_type: "alternative"` makes groups mutually exclusive — only the one named by `selected_option_id` counts:

```
  12000   base work
+ 145000  Option A (selected)
     ---  Option B 78000 quoted but excluded
-  18000  copper salvage (category: material)
= 139000
```

Use `group_type: "additive"` instead when every group should count.

item.name: Validation — expected failures
item.description:
**Every request in this folder is supposed to fail.** They exist to document the error contract, and their tests assert the failure.

A green run here means the API is rejecting bad input correctly.

request.description:

This is the behaviour that makes bulk loads safe: a mis-spelled column fails on row 1 instead of silently vanishing across the whole import.
